physical SQLite table: "emp_hire_periods"
CREATE TABLE "emp_hire_periods" (
  "emp_id" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY; REFERENCES "employees"("id")
  "start_" TEXT -- PRIMARY KEY
  "end_" TEXT
  "title" TEXT
);

physical SQLite table: "employees"
CREATE TABLE "employees" (
  "id" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY
  "name" TEXT
  "title" TEXT
  "supervisor_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "employees"("id")
);

physical SQLite table: "inventory"
CREATE TABLE "inventory" (
  "id" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY
  "location_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "locations"("id")
  "product_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "products"("id")
  "purchase_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "purchases"("id")
  "qty" REAL
);

physical SQLite table: "locations"
CREATE TABLE "locations" (
  "id" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY
  "warehouse" INTEGER
  "aisle" TEXT
  "position" INTEGER
);

physical SQLite table: "orderlines"
CREATE TABLE "orderlines" (
  "id" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY
  "order_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "orders"("id")
  "product_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "products"("id")
  "qty" REAL
  "amount" REAL
);

physical SQLite table: "orders"
CREATE TABLE "orders" (
  "id" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY
  "customer_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "customers"("id")
  "ordered" TEXT
  "delivery" TEXT
);

physical SQLite table: "picking_line"
CREATE TABLE "picking_line" (
  "picklist_id" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY; REFERENCES "picking_list"("id")
  "line_no" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY
  "location_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "locations"("id")
  "order_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "orders"("id")
  "product_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "products"("id")
  "qty" REAL
);

physical SQLite table: "picking_log"
CREATE TABLE "picking_log" (
  "picklist_id" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY; REFERENCES "picking_list"("id")
  "log_time" TEXT -- PRIMARY KEY
  "activity" TEXT
  "location_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "locations"("id")
  "pickline_no" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "picking_line"("line_no")
);

physical SQLite table: "purchases"
CREATE TABLE "purchases" (
  "id" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY
  "purchased" TEXT
  "brewery_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "breweries"("id")
  "product_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "products"("id")
  "qty" INTEGER
  "cost" REAL
);

physical SQLite table: "web_counter_hist"
CREATE TABLE "web_counter_hist" (
  "app_id" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY; REFERENCES "web_pages"("app_id")
  "page_no" INTEGER -- PRIMARY KEY; REFERENCES "web_pages"("page_no")
  "day" TEXT -- PRIMARY KEY
  "counter" INTEGER
);

physical SQLite table: "web_demographics"
CREATE TABLE "web_demographics" (
  "day" unknown -- PRIMARY KEY
  "m_tw_cnt" INTEGER
  "m_tw_qty" INTEGER
  "m_fb_cnt" INTEGER
  "m_fb_qty" INTEGER
  "f_tw_cnt" INTEGER
  "f_tw_qty" INTEGER
  "f_fb_cnt" INTEGER
  "f_fb_qty" INTEGER
);

physical SQLite table: "web_devices"
CREATE TABLE "web_devices" (
  "day" unknown -- PRIMARY KEY
  "pc" INTEGER
  "tablet" INTEGER
  "phone" INTEGER
);

physical SQLite table: "web_page_visits"
CREATE TABLE "web_page_visits" (
  "client_ip" TEXT
  "visit_time" TEXT
  "app_id" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "web_pages"("app_id")
  "page_no" INTEGER -- REFERENCES "web_pages"("page_no")
);

cases.title: What is the average total quantity across all final packaging combinations,
cases.question: What is the average total quantity across all final packaging combinations, considering only the leaf-level items within each combination after fully expanding any nested packaging relationships?

cases.title: Which top-level packaging containers, meaning those not contained within an
cases.question: Which top-level packaging containers, meaning those not contained within any other packaging, have any item for which the total quantity accumulated across all nested levels in the hierarchy exceeds 500, and what are the names of both these containers and the corresponding items?

cases.title: For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which t
cases.question: For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which to pick the exact quantities needed for each order line, ensuring that the total picked quantity for each product matches the cumulative quantities ordered without exceeding the available inventory in warehouse 1. Calculate the quantities to be picked from each location by prioritizing inventory with earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities, and ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries.

cases.title: Calculate the average pick percentage for each product name, using a first-
cases.question: Calculate the average pick percentage for each product name, using a first-in-first-out approach that selects from inventory locations based on the earliest purchase date and smallest available quantity, ensuring that the picked quantity reflects only the overlapping range between each order’s required quantity and the inventory’s available quantity, and then grouping and ordering the results by product name?

cases.title: Which products were picked for order 421, and what is the average number of
cases.question: Which products were picked for order 421, and what is the average number of units picked for each product, using FIFO (First-In, First-Out) method?

cases.title: Based on monthly sales data starting in January 2016 and using a centered m
cases.question: Based on monthly sales data starting in January 2016 and using a centered moving average to adjust for seasonality, which products had a seasonality-adjusted sales ratio that stayed consistently above 2 for every month in the year 2017?

cases.title: What is the average forecasted annual sales for products 4160 and 7790 duri
cases.question: What is the average forecasted annual sales for products 4160 and 7790 during 2018, using monthly sales data starting from January 2016 for the first 36 months, applying seasonality adjustments from time steps 7 through 30, and employing a weighted regression method to estimate sales?

cases.title: Using a recursive monthly inventory adjustment model starting from December
cases.question: Using a recursive monthly inventory adjustment model starting from December 2018 inventory levels, where we restock a product if its ending inventory drops below the minimum required level, determine for each product the month in 2019 where the absolute difference between its ending inventory and the minimum required level is the smallest, and return the product_id, that month, and the absolute difference.
